notes:
Overview: Mid-size omnichannel retailer focusing on catalog search relevance + conversion lift. Very sensitive to cost per query during seasonal spikes. 

Key facts (from discovery):
- Catalog: ~3.2M SKUs, ~400 attributes (variants, color, size, vendor meta). Avg product doc ~1.2KB after normalization.
- Traffic: baseline ~200 qps (global), daily ~5M queries. Peak targets: Black Friday/Cyber week projected peak ~1.5k-1.8k qps sustained for 8-12 hours (spike pattern).
- Current stack: Elasticsearch for faceted and cheap BM25 retrieval; experiments with Pinecone for embeddings but cost + latency uncertain at scale.

Technical requirements / goals:
- Primary workload: hybrid retrieval (BM25 candidate set) + embedding-based reranking for semantic match + personalization signals.
- Indexing scale: need bulk reindexing pipeline that can handle full rebuild within 24-36 hours for 3M docs; incremental updates <100k/day.
- Latency SLOs: p95 end-to-end (retrieve + rerank) <= 150ms preferred, hard cap 250ms for product listing responses.
- Cost target: aim <$0.002 per query (retrieval+rerank) averaged across baseline; accept higher for peak but want predictable unit economics.
- Model constraints: prefer smaller quantized rerankers (distilled or 8-bit) for cost; open to Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.
- Fallbacks: must have deterministic fallback to BM25-only results when model options or capacity limited.

Security & compliance:
- Data residency: EU catalog subset must remain in eu-west region for some customers.
- SSO + RBAC mandatory for admin console; audit logs required for product changes.
- KMS integration for any secret keys; legal to sign addendum for dataset handling.

Engagement timeline / recent activity:
- 2024-11-05: Intro call (AE: Alex) — high-level needs, agreed to technical deep-dive.
- 2024-11-19: SE session (Priya) — reviewed indexing characteristics, sample payloads shared (drive link). Action: Redwood to propose batching strategy and cost calc.
- 2024-11-28: Security questionnaire submitted (drive link); Redwood asked to provide SOC2 + retention controls answers.
- 2024-12-05: Scale planning call (Fireflies ff_1842_ecom-poc-call-20241205) — discussed 1M-doc POC and synthetic load test (100k queries).
- 2024-12-10: Pricing follow-up (AE) — customer asked for per-q cost comparison Hosted vs Dedicated for Black Friday 8-hour window at 1.6k qps.

POC plan (agreed scope):
- Phase 1 (week 1): Index 1M SKUs into Redwood Dedicated test cluster (subset of EU + NA). Run 100k synthetic queries representing typical session patterns. Measure: indexing throughput, p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates, per-query token cost.
- Phase 2 (week 2): Scale to 3M in staging (if Phase 1 passes), run load pattern that simulates sustained 1.5k qps for 8 hours. Validate autoscaling/burst behavior and canary fallbacks.
- Deliverables: detailed cost-per-query spreadsheet, latency percentiles, recommended batching/quantization profile from Redwood Optimize.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "If we can't show <$0.002/q at our scale, tough sell to finance." — Head of Search (call 11/05).
- "Need a deterministic rollback plan for peak day — no surprises, degrade to BM25 if model cpu saturated." — CTO.

Open items / blockers:
- Legal needs confirmation: EU data residency mapping for segmented SKUs (SEC-4479).
- Engineering asks a proof of concept for quantized reranker (8-bit) with sample throughput numbers.
- Pricing: require an example bill for a 8-hour 1.6k qps Black Friday event (differentiated Hosted vs Dedicated).

Next immediate steps (short):
- Deliver POC runbook and cost model (Alex/Priya) by 2024-12-13.
- Kick off Phase 1 indexing POC (target start 2024-12-18).
- Arrange security deep-dive w/ Security team to clear data residency questions (SEC-4479).
